title: helm: private - tighten values schema, add initJobs and pre-upgrade hooks for private installer
author: Maya Chen
commits: validate(values): add JSON schema for private values and strict type checks
feat(helm): add init job to populate on-prem system namespaces and secrets
feat(helm): add pre-upgrade hook which runs schema+compat checks before upgrade
chore(tests): add upgrade-smoke test and CI job
fix(lint): adjust templates for missing default values
release_notes: Helm chart updates for Redwood Private: stricter values schema validation; new initJob to bootstrap on-prem namespaces and secrets; new pre-upgrade hooks to validate compatibility and prevent unsafe upgrades; added upgrade smoke test. No breaking changes intended; new fields are optional and have defaults.
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem reported upgrade failures caused by missing optional fields and subtle templating assumptions. This PR tightens the values schema, makes templating safer by providing explicit defaults, and adds an idempotent initJob plus Helm pre-upgrade hooks to validate compatibility before performing a chart upgrade. Motivation: reduce field-related upgrade incidents, make private installer more robust in air-gapped and restricted environments, and provide clearer upgrade/rollback safety signals. What changed: 1) charts/private/values.schema.json: added strict types for cpu/memory/quota, storageClass, kms key refs, and added patterns for CIDR and URL fields; 2) charts/private/values.yaml: added documented defaults and examples; 3) templates/init-job.yaml: idempotent Kubernetes Job that creates namespaces, populates initial secrets (TLS, service account token bootstrap) when missing; runs as an annotation-driven init that can be disabled via values.private.init.enabled=false; 4) templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-job.yaml and pre-delete-job.yaml: hook jobs that run lightweight compatibility checks against live cluster resources and fail the upgrade if incompatible changes are detected; 5) templates/deployment.yaml: safer use of default values and nil checks around volume mounts to avoid template rendering errors; 6) tests/upgrade-smoke.yaml: CI smoke test exercising upgrade path. Backwards compatibility: default values preserve previous behavior; schema is validation-only (helm lint + test) and will not block installs unless the user opts into stricter CI. Upgrade notes: the pre-upgrade hook will run automatically during helm upgrade; it can be skipped with --no-hooks in emergency but is recommended. Rollback: init job is idempotent; hooks are non-destructive but will be reverted as part of standard Helm rollback. Checklist: - [x] values schema added and validated via helm schema lint - [x] initJob implemented and tested locally - [x] pre-upgrade/pre-delete hooks implemented - [x] CI smoke test added - [x] reviewers addressed comments Summary of review conversation: Carlos asked to make KMS key and vault refs optional and allowed empty strings; author updated schema and added pattern checking and example values. Priya requested the initJob use RBAC with minimal privileges; author reduced permissions and scoped ServiceAccount, added comment in README. Evan flagged a potential race between initJob and operator start; author added an annotation-driven wait and a short retry loop in the init job to avoid races. CI: initial lint job failed due to missing example values; fixed and rerun; final CI status: pass. Testing: local k3s + GKE staging upgrade tested; added upgrade-smoke job to CI pipeline. Merge: approved by all reviewers, merged via squash on 2026-02-18. Notes for operators: if you have highly customized values, run `helm template` with the new schema and run `kubectl apply -f` the init job output in a staging cluster before upgrading production. If pre-upgrade hook fails, inspect hook pod logs (kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<name>) for compatibility errors. Related work: ENG-2345 tracks broader installer hardening and SUP-1023 is the customer incident that prompted this change.
